comparator.name: Tax Law
comparator.sourceNotes: Checked 2026-11-13. Current BA-FIS retains revised years 1/2: 24 required 5 EC units = 120 EC. Adopted 2026–2027 OER 2.4/2.5 and 3.1/3.2 establish three years, 180 EC, 150 required plus 30 open EC. Footnote 17 distinguishes entrants before 2025; 3.2.3–3.2.6 govern level, approval and non-overlap, with Honours excluded. The revised diagram names six third-year spring units and explicitly weights Moot Court Tax Law at 5 EC. Retain 26 supported components totalling 155 EC, including genuine 30 EC open space; remaining 25 required EC lack a revised-cohort individual allocation. Current catalogue year 3 is explicitly for entrants in 2024 or earlier. Seven actual current module records provide useful 5 EC weights, specialist tax-law content, thesis and entry rules for that outgoing structure, but no explicit revised-cohort bridge. The forward-year request returns the same current record. OER 3.3.2 and 4.2.1 still delegate final-work standards and mandatory order to the guide. Do not infer equal revised weights, import the outgoing thesis or treat Moot Court as its replacement. Current curriculum overview and transition table do not establish that bridge. Existing verified 60 interest classifications and 18 current-UCR contribution findings remain relevant; no complete comparison, no-match or professional equivalence is inferred. LLP/tutoring/language-test placeholders add no credits.

audience.programmeDescription: Leiden’s Tax Law bachelor studies how taxes work in law, business and society. Students combine legal interpretation and argument with economics, financial accounting and ethical questions about taxation. Teaching is in Dutch, with some English.
audience.comparisonExplanation: A complete comparison with UCR is awaiting confirmation of the revised third-year requirements. No UCR alternative is presented while this academic assessment remains unfinished.
